title: ChroSpin - IMAC
author: Alexandra Ehl
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tv3en8n
materials: Deionized water Cleaning solution 1: 6 M Guanidine chloride, 0.2 M Acetic acid Cleaning solution 2: 1 % Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) Cleaning solution 3: > 95 % Ethanol Cleaning solution 4: 0.1 M Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) Cleaning solution 5: 0.2 M Acetic Acid Metal solution: 0.1 M Nickel(II) sulfate (or other metal ion of your choice) 20 % (v/v) Ethanol

steps.title: Prepare buffers
steps.instruction: Make the wash and elution buffers with the exact concentrations listed, adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH, and handle urea‑containing buffers freshly.

substeps.instruction: Wash buffer: 0.05 M sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 4 M urea, 0.3 M sodium chloride; adjust to pH 8.0 with NaOH.
Elution buffer: 0.05 M sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 4 M urea, 0.250 M sodium chloride, imidazole; adjust to pH 8.0 with NaOH.
Buffers containing urea are unstable at room temperature – prepare on the day of use, store aliquots at –20 °C for no longer than two months and do not freeze‑thaw more than once.

steps.title: Resuspend bacterial pellet
steps.instruction: Weigh the frozen pellet, thaw it on ice (or at room temperature if preferred), and resuspend in wash buffer at 3–5 mL per gram of pellet.

substeps.instruction: Add lysozyme and DNase I at 0.01 % (mass/volume) each, corresponding to 0.1 mg mL⁻¹ each.
If preferred, substitute enzymatic lysis with ultrasonication according to the instrument’s instructions and skip the enzymatic addition step.
Pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cells with gentle mixing
steps.instruction: Incubate the resuspended cells with end‑over‑end mixing (or gentle rocking) under the appropriate temperature and time conditions.

substeps.instruction: For standard proteins: 30 min at 22 °C (room temperature).
If the target protein is prone to proteolysis: 60 min at 4–8 °C.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate for 30 min at >10 000 g at 4 °C, then carefully transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.

substeps.instruction: During this centrifugation you may begin column equilibration steps.

steps.title: Load metal onto column
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of nickel or cobalt solution to the spin column, close the lid, and incubate 1 min with end‑over‑end mixing.

substeps.instruction: Note: Cu²⁺ and Zn²⁺ can also be used. Affinity order: Cu > Ni > Zn > Co; specificity order is the inverse.

steps.title: Initial column centrifugation
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom lid, centrifuge the column at 1000 g for 30–60 s, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with deionized water (twice)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL deionized water, close the lid, invert sharply 3–5 times, centrifuge at 1000 g for 30–60 s, discard flow‑through, and repeat once more.

steps.title: Equilibrate with wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer, close the lid, invert sharply 3–5 times, and centrifuge at 1000 g for 30–60 s.

steps.title: Load lysate onto column
steps.instruction: Place the column in a fresh collection tube, add up to 500 µL cleared lysate, close the lid, and incubate 5 min with end‑over‑end mixing.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1000 g for 30–60 s and collect the flow‑through.
If the total lysate volume exceeds 500 µL, repeat the loading cycle until all lysate is applied.
Retain flow‑through and wash fractions for later analysis (e.g., SDS‑PAGE).

steps.title: Wash column with wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL wash buffer, close the lid, invert sharply 3–5 times, centrifuge at 1000 g for 30–60 s, and empty the collection tube.

substeps.instruction: Repeat once more without changing the collection tube.
For higher purity, repeat the wash up to a total of five times.

steps.title: Elute target protein
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL elution buffer to the column, centrifuge at 1000 g for 30–60 s, and collect the eluate.

substeps.instruction: Without changing the collection tube, repeat the elution step two additional times (total of three 200 µL elutions).

steps.title: Sequential cleaning with cleaning solutions
steps.instruction: If the column will be reused, clean it with the supplied cleaning solutions followed by water washes.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL cleaning solution 1, invert sharply 4–5 times, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL deionized water, invert 4–5 times, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard.
Add a second 500 µL deionized water wash, repeat inversion and centrifugation, discard.
Add 500 µL cleaning solution 2, invert 4–5 times, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard.
Add 500 µL deionized water, invert 4–5 times, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard.
Add a final 500 µL deionized water wash, invert 4–5 times, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard.

steps.title: Final wash and recharge
steps.instruction: Prepare the column for the next use by washing and re‑metalating.

substeps.instruction: Wash the column three times with 500 µL deionized water as described above.
Add 500 µL fresh metal solution, incubate 5 min with end‑over‑end mixing, centrifuge 1 min at 1000 g, discard flow‑through.
Wash the column two additional times with 500 µL deionized water, centrifuging each time at 1000 g for 30–60 s.

steps.title: Store column
steps.instruction: Close the bottom of the column and add 500 µL 20 % ethanol or wash buffer (containing 0.05 % w/v sodium azide).

substeps.instruction: Close the lid and store the column at room temperature or at 4–8 °C.
For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for at least 2 h or overnight, then close and store as above.

steps.title: Sanitize column (optional)
steps.instruction: If sanitization is required, treat the column with sanitization solution.

substeps.instruction: Close the bottom of the column, add 500 µL sanitization solution, close the lid, and incubate 1 h at 22 °C (room temperature).
Remove the bottom cap, centrifuge 30–60 s at 1000 g, and wash three times with 500 µL deionized water (centrifuging each wash).
